content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification: deviation (fails fallback), redlined to preferred.**

- **What exists:** Section 10.3 "Assignment" (p0063) is a bare binding-effect clause — it binds the parties' "legal representatives, successors and assigns" but never states who may assign, contains no consent standard, no affiliate/M&A carve-out for us, and no restriction on HDI assigning (including to a competitor).
- **Change of control:** searches confirm the phrase appears nowhere, and the Section 4 term/termination provisions contain no change-of-control trigger — so HDI has no exit right today, but the point is unconfirmed in the text.
- **Why not fallback-compliant:** none of the fallback elements (mutual successor assignment, written notice, consent for other assignments, reasonableness standard) are present; the clause is silent rather than at the fallback.
- **Cure:** one inserted paragraph in Section 10.3 carrying all six preferred elements (our affiliate/M&A assignment right without consent; no HDI termination on our change of control; HDI assignment only with our consent, not unreasonably withheld, and never to a competitor). The existing sentence is preserved verbatim, and no ancillary boilerplate was added.
